gaps.concept: Gs activates adenylyl cyclase, raising cAMP and protein kinase A activity.
gaps.why_tested: A receptor-signaling stem asks which enzyme or kinase acts downstream of Gs. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK20/)

gaps.concept: Gq activates phospholipase C; IP3 releases calcium, while DAG activates protein kinase C.
gaps.why_tested: A signaling diagram asks for the branch missing from an IP3–calcium pathway. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK538154/)

gaps.concept: Gi-coupled dopamine D2 and somatostatin receptors inhibit adenylyl cyclase and lower cAMP.
gaps.why_tested: A prolactin or growth-hormone stem asks which G protein mediates inhibition. [Sources](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK551686/)

gaps.concept: Dopamine tonically inhibits prolactin; D2 blockade or pituitary stalk disruption increases prolactin.
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops galactorrhea after antipsychotic use or a sellar mass. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537331/)

gaps.concept: Insulin receptor autophosphorylation recruits IRS proteins; PI3K–Akt signaling moves GLUT4 to muscle and adipose cell membranes.
gaps.why_tested: A postprandial glucose-uptake stem asks for the pathway downstream of insulin binding. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK378978/)

gaps.concept: Leptin signals chiefly through a receptor-associated JAK–STAT pathway.
gaps.why_tested: An obesity or appetite-regulation stem asks which receptor-signaling class leptin uses. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537038/)

gaps.concept: Anti-Müllerian hormone and activin signal through serine/threonine kinase receptors and SMAD transcription factors.
gaps.why_tested: A reproductive hormone stem asks for a receptor class absent from the usual GPCR, tyrosine-kinase, and nuclear-receptor choices. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK544351/)

gaps.concept: ANP and BNP activate membrane guanylyl cyclase; nitric oxide activates soluble guanylyl cyclase.
gaps.why_tested: A cGMP stem asks which receptor or enzyme each ligand activates. [Sources](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2647281/)

gaps.concept: Pulsatile GnRH maintains LH and FSH secretion; continuous GnRH agonism causes an initial flare followed by receptor desensitization and suppression.
gaps.why_tested: A GnRH-agonist stem asks why gonadal hormone levels rise briefly, then fall. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279126/)

gaps.concept: Inhibin selectively suppresses FSH; activin stimulates FSH synthesis.
gaps.why_tested: A gonadal-feedback stem asks why FSH changes disproportionately to LH. [Source](https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279031/)

gaps.concept: FSH, LH, TSH, and hCG share an alpha subunit; distinct beta subunits confer specificity, though high hCG can stimulate TSH receptors.
gaps.why_tested: A molar-pregnancy stem pairs very high hCG with thyrotoxicosis. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/n/nap232757/pdf/)

gaps.concept: Primary hormone excess suppresses its trophic hormone; a trophic-hormone-secreting pituitary lesion raises both hormones.
gaps.why_tested: A two-hormone lab pattern asks whether excess production originates in the peripheral gland or pituitary. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK26/)

gaps.concept: Target-organ hormone resistance can produce high peripheral hormone and high trophic hormone despite intact production.
gaps.why_tested: High hormone with unsuppressed trophic hormone suggests impaired receptor response rather than gland failure. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459117/)

gaps.concept: Prolonged exogenous glucocorticoids suppress CRH and ACTH, causing adrenal cortical atrophy.
gaps.why_tested: A chronic steroid-use stem asks why endogenous cortisol remains low after withdrawal. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK13158/)

gaps.concept: Postzygotic activating GNAS mutations cause constitutive Gs–cAMP signaling in McCune–Albright syndrome.
gaps.why_tested: Precocious puberty, irregular café-au-lait patches, and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia identify a signaling defect. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK66130/)

gaps.concept: Maternally inherited inactivating GNAS mutations cause Gs deficiency and resistance to PTH and sometimes other Gs-linked hormones.
gaps.why_tested: Elevated PTH with hypocalcemia and Albright hereditary osteodystrophy prompts identification of the defective signaling protein. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459117/)
